digest.component_or_area: parent-child cascade table and lifecycle invariant enforcement
propositions: The _CASCADING_EDGES table guarantees only per-edge, same-edge parent movement, not a total status ordering or universal 'child never ahead of parent' invariant.
A non-terminal-state ticket must never be a child of a closed ticket (operator-ruled invariant maintained jointly by the table's closed rows and the unconditional close guard in transition_close.py).

Reactivating a closed child under an open parent does not cascade because only a closed parent is eligible on that edge; this residual is documented-intended and pinned by test_reactivate_does_not_disturb_open_parent.

A blocked child resuming to in_progress under an open parent does not cascade (different questions: start-work gate vs same-edge cascade eligibility); the residual is documented non-cascading and pinned by test_blocked_resume_does_not_cascade_open_parent.
The enumerated edge table is retained; ordering-predicate redesign is rejected (AC1 decision ratified by operator reclassification from bug to task).
Documentation, comment/docstring, and test additions reconcile the cascade table behavior with docs/concurrency.md §I4a; table rows and claim-status guard (txn.claim_core) remain unchanged.
